story.title: SpaceX signs deal with Qualcomm to provide network technology for U.S. mobile service - CNBC

facts.text: SpaceX announced a deal with chipmaker Qualcomm to provide key network technology for Elon Musk's Starlink Mobile service, a challenger to Verizon , AT&T and T-Mobile .
Qualcomm said on Wednesday that the terrestrial network it will help SpaceX build will "complement Starlink's satellite capabilities," with a planned rollout to begin next year.
Financial terms of the multiyear deal weren't disclosed.
Starlink is a critical piece of SpaceX's business, accounting for 36% of the company's revenue in the third quarter and 85% of its operating profit.
Now SpaceX is snapping up spectrum and forging partnerships to take on the major mobile carriers.
The news sent shares of U.S. carriers reeling.
Earlier this week, the Washington Post reported that SpaceX is in talks to acquire EchoStar's Boost Mobile.

"Together with SpaceX, we are building world-leading cellular infrastructure in the United States, advancing 5G today, with an opportunity to lay the foundation for AI-native 6G in the years ahead," Durga Malladi, an executive vice president at Qualcomm, said in the statement.
With Qualcomm, SpaceX will be using the chipmaker's Dragonwing cellular infrastructure hardware and software in base stations to enable high-capacity coverage for Starlink Mobile.
SpaceX represents one of Qualcomm's highest-profile customers or partners in 5G infrastructure, following earlier deals with Verizon, Dish, and Europe's Vodafone.
SpaceX did not respond to CNBC's request for additional information.
Qualcomm has a long history of making chips for cellular networks, but is best known for making the modems and radios that go inside devices, not base stations for running a wireless network.
The company has targeted carriers and other infrastructure companies since it made a bigger push into the 5G infrastructure market in 2020 .
While SpaceX plans to use Qualcomm's technology to establish tens of thousands of new cell sites, it hasn't announced partners among cell tower companies or said how many new towers may be required.
SpaceX went public in June in the largest IPO on record and is now valued at close to $2 trillion.

In the United States, SpaceX has signed a multi-year agreement with Qualcomm to supply network technologies for Starlink Mobile base stations, its mobile service intended to compete with Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile.
As CNBC reports , the parties did not disclose the financial terms of the contract.
Qualcomm will provide SpaceX with Dragonwing hardware and software for cellular infrastructure.
Qualcomm said the ground network would complement Starlink's satellite capabilities.
SpaceX plans to use Qualcomm's technologies to create tens of thousands of new cellular sites.
The company did not say which tower operators it would work with or how many new towers would be needed.
Last month, SpaceX also announced an agreement to acquire a nationwide portfolio of spectrum in the 800 MHz band.
Earlier, The Washington Post reported that the company was in talks to buy Boost Mobile from EchoStar.
